newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to turn 20,000 hectares into rice fields.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to turn 20,000 hectares into rice fields.

text.p: Indonesian Planning Minister Ginanjar Kartasasmita said on Friday the government was ready to cultivate rice on 20,000 hectares in Central Kalimantan in the initial phase of project involving 640,000 hectares.
"Some irrigation systems have been completed and we are ready to plant rice in 20,000 hectares," he told reporters after meeting President Suharto.
In 1995, Indonesia proposed to turn one million hectares of peat land in Central Kalimantan into rice fields in a bid to maintain self-sufficiency in rice production.
Ginanjar said some 640,000 hectares would be used to plant rice. The rest would be used for other crops and infrastructure.
"Up till now we have spent 500 billion rupiah to build irrigation systems and in clearing the land," he said.
"We will gradually send transmigrants to the area to plant rice," he said, referring to a participants in a state programme that relocates citizens to under-populated areas.
Transmigration Minister Siswono Yudohusudo said the project was expected to be launched next May.
He said about 10,000 families would be needed to plant rice in the 20,000 hectares. -- Jakarta newsroom 6221 3846364
